newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba insists it wants hijacker returned from U.S.
newsitem.headline: Cuba insists it wants hijacker returned from U.S.

text.p: The Cuban government said on Thursday while it had cooperated in allowing U.S. officials to investigate the hijacking of a Cuban commercial plane to the U.S. Naval Base at Guantanamo Bay, it still wanted the hijacker repatriated.

U.S. officials said on Wednesday an FBI agent and a U.S. Justice Department official were in Cuba this week investigating the hijacking in which former Cuban Interior Ministry official Jose Fernandez Pupo forced a small plane to fly to the U.S. base on the southeast tip of the island on July 7.
Fernandez Pupo asked for political asylum. He is in detention in the United States but U.S. authorities have not said yet what they intend to do with him.

Cuban Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Marianela Ferriol, speaking at a weekly news briefing, said Cuba had cooperated "as a goodwill gesture" in allowing the FBI agent and the U.S. prosecutor to come and investigate the case.

Ferriol said Cuba had agreed through diplomatic channels to allow the investigation. At the same time, she added, Cuba "insisted the real solution (to this case) is for the traitor to be handed back".

Another Foreign Ministry official, North America department deputy head Rafael Dausa, was quoted by the Cuban news agency Prensa Latina as saying the United States government "is apparently pursuing actions with a view to a posssible trial of this criminal".

Dausa added that the investigation by the two U.S. officials was taking place in the eastern province of Santiago de Cuba. The hijacked plane was on a flight around eastern Cuba, including a stop at Santiago de Cuba.
Dausa said Cuba was cooperating with the U.S. officials by providing access to evidence in the case.

Cuban authorities have repeatedly demanded that the hijacker be returned to Cuba, arguing that failure to do so would breach a May 1995 bilateral migration accord. Under this agreement, the United States undertook to repatriate Cubans trying to emigrate to the United States by illegal means, whether by sea or by crossing to the Guantanamo base.

Cuban authorities have also demanded the return of three other Cubans who hijacked a small taxi plane from Cuba towards Florida on August 16. The plane ditched in the Gulf of Florida and the hijackers asked for asylum in the United States after being rescued. The pilot returned home to Cuba.
U.S. authorities have said they plan to try the three Cubans involved in the August incident for air piracy.
